projects.title: Logic and proof technique
projects.blurb: Propositions and truth tables, normal forms, proofs as Lean tactics, quantifiers, three kinds of induction, relations and well-founded termination: the toolkit every later course uses.

lessons.title: Propositions and truth tables
lessons.blurb: Connectives, truth tables, tautologies, and satisfying assignments as witnesses.

lessons.title: Equivalence and normal forms
lessons.blurb: The laws of logic as rewrites: negation normal form, CNF and DNF, one law a step.

lessons.title: Proofs as Lean tactics
lessons.blurb: Natural deduction in Lean: introduce and use each connective, and see proofs as programs.

lessons.title: Predicates and quantifiers
lessons.blurb: ∀ and ∃ over finite sets, with the element that decides them; quantifiers in Lean.

lessons.title: Induction on the natural numbers
lessons.blurb: Weak induction: check a formula for small n, then prove it for all n in Lean.

lessons.title: Strong induction
lessons.blurb: Course-of-values arguments: using every smaller case, and how strong induction, weak induction and well-ordering relate.

lessons.title: Structural induction
lessons.blurb: Induction on lists, trees and expressions, and a small simplifier proved sound.

lessons.title: Relations
lessons.blurb: Properties with counterexamples, closures step by step, equivalence classes and partitions, and a deduplication bug.

lessons.title: Well-founded relations and termination
lessons.blurb: No infinite descent: cycles as counterexamples, measures as proofs, and termination in Lean.

projects.title: Order and lattices
projects.blurb: From Zero to Propagators: partial orders, lattices and fixed points; semilattices as merges, access decisions and information flow; Galois connections; and propagator networks in Lean, ending with a Sudoku solver.

lessons.title: Relations and partial orders
lessons.blurb: Partial orders on numbers, divisibility and sets, Hasse diagrams, and the definitions in Lean.

lessons.title: Special elements and monotone maps
lessons.blurb: Least, greatest, maximal and minimal elements, bounds, joins and meets, and monotone maps.

lessons.title: Lattices
lessons.blurb: Posets where every pair has a join and a meet: duality, the standard examples, and distributivity.

lessons.title: Complete lattices and fixed points
lessons.blurb: Complete lattices, the Knaster–Tarski theorem, and least fixed points by iteration.

lessons.title: Semilattices as algebras
lessons.blurb: Join as an operation with laws: associative, commutative, idempotent, and the order it gives back.

lessons.title: A merge is a join
lessons.blurb: Max, union, last-writer-wins and records merged field by field: why replicas that merge this way agree.

lessons.title: Distributive and Boolean lattices
lessons.blurb: M₃ and N₅ as the witnesses, complements, and the Boolean lattices of sets and squarefree divisors.

lessons.title: Access decisions
lessons.blurb: Combining permit and deny: deny-overrides and permit-overrides are joins, first-applicable is not commutative.

lessons.title: Information flow
lessons.blurb: Denning's lattice of security classes: data may only flow up, and a computation's output gets the join of its inputs' classes.

lessons.title: Closure operators and Galois connections
lessons.blurb: Closure operators, Galois connections between two orders, and the concept lattice of a formal context.

lessons.title: Fixed points in practice
lessons.blurb: Apply until nothing changes: reachability as a least fixed point, and why the iteration stops.

lessons.title: The propagator model
lessons.blurb: Cells that only gain information, in a lattice; propagators as monotone functions between them.

lessons.title: A propagator network in Lean
lessons.blurb: Mutable cells that only grow, a scheduler that runs to quiescence, and a constraint that runs in every direction.

lessons.title: The interval lattice
lessons.blurb: Bounds on a number as partial information: intersection as the merge, and interval arithmetic propagators.

lessons.title: Capstones: Sudoku and type inference
lessons.blurb: A Sudoku solver and a type checker, both as propagator networks over lattices of partial information.

projects.title: CRDTs: replicated data that converges
projects.blurb: From Propagators to Replicas: counters, sets and registers that replicas update without coordinating and merge as joins; the main theorem that they converge; gossip, version vectors, op-based CRDTs, a replicated store, and the limits.

lessons.title: Replicas and the merge discipline
lessons.blurb: Why merging copies is hard, and the one discipline that makes it easy: states in a semilattice, merge as join.

lessons.title: The G-Counter
lessons.blurb: Counting without coordination: one slot per replica, merged by pointwise maximum.

lessons.title: The PN-Counter
lessons.blurb: Counting down without going down: two grow-only counters, and a query that subtracts.

lessons.title: Sets that only grow
lessons.blurb: G-Set and 2P-Set: union as the merge, finite sets as sorted lists, and the removal that cannot be undone.

lessons.title: Last writer wins
lessons.blurb: Overwrite, done lawfully: timestamps in the state, ties broken by replica, and the LWW-Element-Set.

lessons.title: The OR-Set: add wins
lessons.blurb: Observed-remove: a remove deletes only the adds it has seen, so a concurrent add survives.

lessons.title: Multisets, folds and the main theorem
lessons.blurb: Quotient types for 'the same updates, in any order', and strong eventual consistency proved once for every CRDT.

lessons.title: Delivery: gossip, duplication and reordering
lessons.blurb: A trace semantics for an at-least-once network, eventual delivery implies convergence, and a gossip driver that provably stops.

lessons.title: Version vectors and causality
lessons.blurb: Time without clocks: the G-Counter again, read as a causal history, and concurrency as incomparability.

lessons.title: Op-based CRDTs
lessons.blurb: Shipping operations instead of states: commutativity moves from the merge to the operations, and duplication becomes the network's problem.

lessons.title: Capstone: a replicated store
lessons.blurb: A collaborative shopping list from the course's parts: an OR-Set of items, each with a PN-Counter quantity, converging with no new proofs.

lessons.title: What CRDTs cannot do
lessons.blurb: Agreement is not correctness: invariants that need coordination, and the axiom audit.

projects.title: Transition systems, invariants and temporal logic
projects.blurb: State machines and their reachable states; invariants with counterexample traces and inductive proofs; mutual exclusion, safety and liveness under fairness; temporal logic as fixed points; happens-before, effectively-once delivery, and refinement; rewriting systems, and retries under failure.

lessons.title: State machines and executions
lessons.blurb: Variables, an initial condition and guarded actions; executions as traces; the graph of reachable states.

lessons.title: Invariants and induction
lessons.blurb: Properties of every reachable state: refuted by a shortest trace, proved by induction, and strengthened when induction fails.

lessons.title: Mutual exclusion
lessons.blurb: A check-then-act race as a stepped trace, the fix, its inductive proof, and the same model in TLA+.

lessons.title: Safety and liveness
lessons.blurb: Nothing bad happens; something good eventually does. Deadlocks, lassos, and weak and strong fairness.

lessons.title: Temporal logic as fixed points
lessons.blurb: EF, AF, EG and AG on the lattice of state sets: least and greatest fixed points, computed by Kleene iteration.

lessons.title: Happens-before
lessons.blurb: Events of several processes as a partial order, vector clocks that compute it, and concurrency as incomparability.

lessons.title: Effectively-once delivery
lessons.blurb: A channel that duplicates; a handler that is idempotent keeps the effect exactly once, one that is not double-applies.

lessons.title: Refinement
lessons.blurb: An implementation's steps are the specification's steps or stutters; and a normalization of operations proved sound.

lessons.title: Rewriting systems
lessons.blurb: The normalization of lesson 8 as rules on terms: rewriting to a normal form, termination by a measure, and confluence by critical pairs.

lessons.title: Retries and backoff
lessons.blurb: Retrying a call that fails at random: the chance that every attempt fails, the expected number of attempts, and the load and wait that backoff trades.

projects.title: Calculus: derivatives and integrals
projects.blurb: The rules of differentiation and the chain rule; the circle behind cos, sin and e^(it); tangent lines; then antiderivatives the engine checks by differentiating, definite integrals and Riemann sums.

lessons.title: The rules of differentiation
lessons.blurb: Powers, sums, constant multiples and products: four rules, every step named.

lessons.title: The chain rule
lessons.blurb: Functions of functions: the outer derivative times the inner one, with a slider to watch the inner factor.

lessons.title: Circles, exponentials and rotation
lessons.blurb: Why e^(it) walks round the unit circle: cosine and sine as shadows, multiplying by i as a quarter turn, Euler's formula, angles that add, and arctan as an angle.

lessons.title: Higher derivatives and tangent lines
lessons.blurb: Derivatives of derivatives, slopes at a point, and the tangent line that follows a slider.

lessons.title: Antiderivatives, checked
lessons.blurb: Integration as the search for a function whose derivative you know, accepted only after the engine differentiates it back.

lessons.title: Definite integrals and sums
lessons.blurb: The fundamental theorem of calculus, finite sums, and Riemann sums that close in on the area as a slider adds rectangles.

projects.title: Linear algebra: vectors, matrices and systems
projects.blurb: Vectors and the dot product, matrix arithmetic, solving systems by row reduction with verified row operations, and determinants.

lessons.title: Vectors and the dot product
lessons.blurb: Adding and scaling vectors, lengths, and the dot product that measures angles.

lessons.title: Matrices
lessons.blurb: Matrix arithmetic, the product that is not commutative, the transpose, and a matrix acting on a vector.

lessons.title: Solving systems by row reduction
lessons.blurb: An augmented matrix, the three row operations (each proved to keep the solutions), and reading the answer off the reduced form.

lessons.title: Determinants
lessons.blurb: The determinant of 2×2 and 3×3 matrices, the product rule, and what a zero determinant means.

projects.title: λ-calculus I: computing with functions
projects.blurb: Terms, free and bound variables, substitution without capture, β-reduction and normal forms, evaluation strategies, de Bruijn indices, Church encodings and recursion by fixed points; an interpreter built in Lean alongside.

lessons.title: Terms and notation
lessons.blurb: Variables, functions and applications; how terms are written and read; a first β-step.

lessons.title: Free and bound variables
lessons.blurb: Which variables a λ binds, which are free, and why the names of bound ones do not matter.

lessons.title: Substitution and capture
lessons.blurb: Putting a term in for a variable, without capturing its free variables.

lessons.title: β-reduction and normal forms
lessons.blurb: Reducing to normal form; terms that never stop; why the normal form is unique; η.

lessons.title: Evaluation strategies
lessons.blurb: Which redex next: normal order, call by name, call by value, applicative order.

lessons.title: De Bruijn indices
lessons.blurb: Terms without bound names: indices count the λs, and α-equivalence becomes equality.

lessons.title: Church encodings
lessons.blurb: Booleans, numbers, arithmetic, pairs and lists, built from functions alone.

lessons.title: Recursion and fixed points
lessons.blurb: No names, yet recursion: fixed-point combinators, factorial, and Y under call by value.

projects.title: λ-calculus II: types and proofs
projects.blurb: The simply typed λ-calculus: typing rules and derivation trees, type inference by unification, what types rule out, propositions as types, type safety, polymorphism and dependent types, with the theory proved in Lean.

lessons.title: Simple types
lessons.blurb: Types for terms: base types and arrows, annotated binders, and the three typing rules.

lessons.title: Typing derivations
lessons.blurb: Contexts and judgments, why a term fails to type, and the checker proved sound.

lessons.title: Type inference
lessons.blurb: Types without annotations: type variables, equations, unification and the occurs check.

lessons.title: What types rule out
lessons.blurb: No Ω, no Y: typed terms always stop. The cost, and a typed language that cannot loop.

lessons.title: Propositions as types
lessons.blurb: A type is a proposition, a term of it a proof: the Curry–Howard correspondence.

lessons.title: Type safety
lessons.blurb: Well-typed programs do not go wrong: progress and preservation, and a safety proof in Lean.

lessons.title: Polymorphism
lessons.blurb: One term at many types: type schemes, System F, and Church numerals that work at every type.

lessons.title: Dependent types
lessons.blurb: Types that depend on values; Lean's type theory; type checking is proof checking.

projects.title: Explorations
projects.blurb: Notebooks that show what ChalkMath does: a tour, Fourier series drawing a llama, and order theory with its proofs in Lean.

lessons.title: Welcome to ChalkMath
lessons.blurb: A short tour: running cells, reading the steps, and one example from each area.

lessons.title: Drawing llamas with circles
lessons.blurb: Fourier series from inner products to epicycles, ending with a llama drawn by spinning circles.

lessons.title: Order and lattices
lessons.blurb: Part I of From Zero to Propagators: partial orders, joins and meets, monotone maps and fixed points, with the proofs in Lean cells.
